question: Which added readout can distinguish time-dependent recovery of a drug-tolerant state from a constant-rate alternative after allowing the constant-rate model to fit the same early observations?
scope: Synthetic experiment-design stress test; no patient data fitting, doses, treatment scheduling, validated biomarker, or new biological mechanism claim.

hypotheses.H0: Post-stress P-to-S switching has constant rate b, estimated as a nuisance parameter from each virtual experiment.
hypotheses.H1: Post-stress exit recovers gradually: b(t)=b_inf*(1-exp(-t/tau)); this is a phenomenological memory alternative, not an established molecular mechanism.

time_unit: One hypothetical sensitive-cell doubling time; no conversion to days is justified.
known_initial_observations: Both models share exactly the same stress-endpoint N0=1 and F0=f0. These initial values and gS,gP are treated as known in the primary design, an idealization.

model_parameters.source_status: All numbers are hypothetical sensitivity values, not estimated from papers, Iowa records or GSE292469.

noise_model: Independent mean-unbiased lognormal burden errors; independent binomial state counts with known symmetric label error. No demographic or replicate heterogeneity is simulated; power may be optimistic.
null_fit: Minimize joint count/binomial deviance over b in a fixed uniform grid from0 to1.6 with321 points; estimate separately in every simulated replicate.

null_calibration.critical_value: Maximum empirical95th-percentile deviance over calibration b-grid, independently for each design/f0/gP/noise combination. This only controls the specified grid and assumptions.

heldout_null.report: False-positive proportion and binomial Monte Carlo standard error for each case; no claim of uniform mathematical type-I control.

alternative_power.report: Reject-constant-rate frequency, not probability of a biological mechanism.

specificity_stress_test: For every noiseless alternative fit a memoryless model with both b and gP free to the two total-count observations; record whether it mimics both counts, and held-out phenotype/third-time count discrepancies. This is an alternate explanation, not validation.
controls: Constant b solved analytically and compared with ODE integration.
Equal growth gS=gP makes total N exactly exp(gS*t) regardless of switching; no total-count design can identify memory.
Vanishing tau converges to constant-b alternative.
No P population gives no switching-dependent signal.
Primary false-positive performance must be reported beside power.
novelty: Memory/state-switching models and measurement-based identifiability are established prior art. Novelty of this exact stress-test design is unestablished; useful output is a reproducible quantitative measurement comparison under explicit assumptions.

design_comparison_limit: Designs differ in measurement modality and number of readouts; no cost-normalized or universally optimal design claim. State fractions require a validated functional phenotype assay, not merely the17-gene score.
summary_reporting: Report all81 parameter cases per noise setting/design, max/min/median power and count of primary cases with at least80percent power; this is descriptive simulation performance, not an empirical biological threshold.
